description: A plain function such as CanActivateFn that the router calls before activating a route and that returns a boolean, a UrlTree or an Observable or Promise of either.
A parsed destination that a guard returns to redirect the navigation instead of simply blocking it.
401 means the server does not know who is calling and 403 means it knows and refuses, so a client treats them differently.
The combination of scheme, host and port, where a difference in any of the three makes a request cross-origin.
The browser rule that a script may read a cross-origin response only when the server opts in with Access-Control-Allow-Origin and related headers.
The OPTIONS request a browser sends before a non-simple cross-origin request to ask whether the server allows the real one.
A rule in proxy.conf.json that makes the dev server forward /api/** to the back end, so the browser only sees its own origin.
